content.title: Management of patients receiving potential cardiotoxic treatments

flowchart_summary.before_treatment: Baseline risk assessment including clinical assessment, ECG, resting echocardiogram and cardiac biomarkers (NP, troponin). Identify pre-existing heart failure or high-risk cardiovascular disease.
flowchart_summary.risk_stratification: Patients classified as medium- and high-risk versus low-risk.

during_treatment.medium_high_risk: Increased surveillance with ECG and cardiac biomarkers during treatment. Reassessment at 3 months and 12 months after completion of cancer therapy.
during_treatment.low_risk: Standard surveillance during treatment. Reassessment at 12 months after completion of cancer therapy.

flowchart_summary.after_treatment: Surveillance every 5 years following therapies with established cardiotoxicity (e.g., high-dose anthracycline chemotherapy). Follow-up by heart failure or cardio-oncology team for new heart failure or left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

surveillance_timing_notes.long_term_follow_up: Yearly/5-yearly clinical review every 5 years with history, examination, NP and troponin levels, and echocardiogram.

abbreviations_expanded.HFA-ICOS: HFA-ICOS baseline cardiovascular risk proformas (Heart Failure Association - International Cardio-Oncology Society)

content.references_notes: Figure 18 from ESC guideline page showing management algorithm and footnotes describing surveillance intervals and examples of cardiotoxic therapies.
